inputs.source: HR-maintained published policy documents, read-only to the agent

instructions.note: The directive not to give legal advice is enforced only by model compliance with a prompt instruction; no structural classifier or filter backs it up.

elements.name: Policy document content flow into search

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by HR publishing process outside the model and does not depend on model capability. It reduces the likelihood of malicious content entering the index but does not constrain any sink, so it earns no residual tier credit under rubric step 3.

controls.name: Agent credential is read-only and scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: A read-only IAM scope enforced outside the model; no model behavior can grant write or delete access the credential lacks.

controls.name: Network egress denied at the network layer, verified by penetration test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer and verified by a pen test; no model behavior can open a network path that does not exist.

controls.name: Reply destination bound to the originating authenticated session; no link/image rendering
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is fixed by the chat transport to the originating authenticated session, not chosen by the model, and the client does not render links or images, closing common side-channel exfiltration vectors.

controls.name: SSO authentication of employee chat sessions
Model version pinned; change requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning requires a change ticket before the model version can change, converting the model_upgrade trigger into a reviewable event rather than a silent occurrence.

controls.name: System prompt scope and disclosure instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model following prompt instructions (quote policy, disclaim when unanswered, avoid legal advice). A more capable model presented with injected instructions in retrieved content may rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: No structural check that served policy content matches the two-person-approved version
No attributable, tamper-evident record of policy_search queries or chat replies
No stated rate, step, or runtime limit on policy_search or chat replies

findings.title: Internally-sourced policy content reaches the employee reply with no structural content-integrity check beyond publish-time review

attack_path.note: HR-authored, two-person-reviewed policy content, not authored by the requesting employee
Agent searches and reads the policy index
Content is quoted verbatim into the reply per prompt.md:2

threat_refs.name: Context Memory Poisoning via Vector Store Contamination

evidence.observation: Policy index holds only published policies; write access is restricted to the HR content team with two-person review before publish, which reduces but does not structurally eliminate the chance of malicious or mistaken content entering the index.

The prompt instructs the agent to use policy_search and quote the relevant policy, so any text injected into a published policy document would be quoted directly into the reply with no stated structural filtering.

cap.chat_reply is classified as sink class S1 rather than the literal 'write on internal data' default of S2: it only delivers already-read internal content back to the same authenticated requester who asked the question, is_egress is false, and no persistent business record is created beyond the ephemeral chat transcript. This judgment is recorded here per SKILL.md rule 4.

recommendations.action: Add provenance or hash verification so the agent only serves content matching the two-person-approved version, and spotlight retrieved policy content as data distinct from instructions.

forecast.watch_signal: New entries in the tool manifest that add a network-reaching action (email, webhook, ticket comment, API call), or new content sources feeding the policy index without the two-person review gate.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions and no rate, step, or runtime limit

evidence.observation: No mention of logging, audit trail, rate limiting, or step/runtime caps anywhere in the artifacts.
The system prompt contains no reference to logging obligations or usage limits.

recommendations.action: Add tamper-evident logging of policy_search queries and chat replies tied to the authenticated employee identity.
Add an explicit per-session or per-day rate limit on policy_search calls as defense in depth.

forecast.watch_signal: New tool or capability additions that write, delete, execute, spend, delegate, or access credentials, added without a corresponding audit log or rate/step limit.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent itself authenticates to the chat platform or policy index beyond stating a scoped credential, so spoofing of the agent's own identity cannot be assessed.
The agent has no configure capability and autonomy.can_modify_own_config is false, so no input can tamper with the agent's own configuration or prompt.
Artifacts do not state whether the chat platform retains session logs tying replies to specific authenticated employees over time.
Artifacts state two-person review is required before publishing but do not confirm reviewer identities are recorded for each publish decision.
Artifacts do not state query rate limits or capacity protections for the policy index itself.

rating.rationale: Two present findings were identified. F1: internally-sourced policy content (two-person reviewed, not the principal's own instruction) reaches the employee chat reply with no structural content-integrity check; F2: no attributable record of actions and no rate/step/runtime limit. Both are inherent and residual 'low' because the only sink reachable from any input is a read of internal policy content delivered back to the same authenticated requester, with no egress, execute, write-to-store, spend, delegation, or credential-access capability present; destination binding and network egress denial (verified by pen test) sever any path to a third party. cap.chat_reply was scored as sink class S1 rather than the literal 'write' default of S2 because it only returns already-read internal content to the same authenticated requester with is_egress false and no persistent record created, a judgment recorded in finding.f1's evidence per SKILL.md rule 4. The forecast rises to 'high' because today's only defense against injected instructions in policy content is a human two-person review process with no structural provenance check; if a future tool or data-scope change adds a write-, execute-, or egress-capable sink, this same content-trust gap becomes a genuine tampering or exfiltration path, and the current network/destination controls would need to be explicitly extended to the new channel.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No explicit numeric step count or runtime limit is stated for the agent; the absence was treated as a missing-property finding (F2) rather than triggering the inherent-risk autonomy modifier, since the system prompt describes a single bounded search-and-reply interaction with no looping, delegation, or self-spawning capability.
No MCP, A2A, or formal protocol configuration was provided; tools.json is treated as a simple internal tool manifest rather than a verified protocol connection.
The efficacy of the two-person policy review process and the existence of chat/identity platform logs are declared facts, not independently verified evidence.
